**Repaired finding submitted: deviation, with a validated redline (ok:true).**

What changed from my earlier call, and why:

- **Affiliate coverage fails the fallback.** §1.4 grants access and the right to use the hosting system and admin tools to "the Company" only — no Affiliates, no contractors, and no written-notice mechanic to add them. That is a material fallback term unmet.
- **My prior premise was wrong.** I had treated the silence as permissive, but §10.3 — the same paragraph I relied on for successor transfer — says "no other person shall acquire or have any rights under this Agreement," which affirmatively excludes Affiliates and contractors and leaves no path to add them. That is the rule's walk-away trigger, not a neutral gap.
- **§10.3 is only a binding-effect clause.** It confirms the Agreement inures to successors but grants no affirmative right to transfer the licence in an M&A transaction, so it weakly supports the second fallback limb and cannot cure the affiliate gap.

Redline (preferred level, precedent seed-license):
1. §1.4 — grant now runs to "the Company, its Affiliates and its contractors acting on its behalf" for both the system and the admin tools.
2. §10.3 — carve-out so Affiliates/contractors may exercise the §1.4 rights, plus an express right to assign to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets.

The [Playbook] comment explains both edits and offers the written-notice fallback. Revocability needed no change — the grant is not revocable at HDI's discretion.
